title: Bounded-below continuity for open direct image and closed support
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, put $B_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and use the ordinary uncompleted category $D(B_T)=D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $T$ be a scheme with Noetherian underlying topological space (descending chains of closed subsets stabilize), $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ closed and $j:U\hookrightarrow T$ its open complement [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use $Rj_*$ and $Ri^!$ from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement], with $Ri^!$ the derived right adjoint of $i_*$. All sites and indexing categories are small in the fixed module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Filtered colimits below are termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives, and all comparison maps are induced by the original cocone. For every small filtered diagram $(N_i)$ of $B_T$-module complexes with $H^{<c}(N_i)=0$, and every such diagram $(V_i)$ on $U$ with $H^{<c}(V_i)=0$, the natural maps
$$\varinjlim_i Ri^!N_i\longrightarrow Ri^!(\varinjlim_iN_i),\qquad \varinjlim_iRj_*V_i\longrightarrow Rj_*(\varinjlim_iV_i)$$
are isomorphisms. Both functors preserve $D^{\ge c}$ for every integer $c$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. No local Noetherianity of the structure sheaf, cohomological dimension bound or constructibility of the targets is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact); agent support-triangle extraction of the bounded-below route in Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 6.3.14 and 6.8.12, using det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image.

proof.text: Interpret each $B_S$-module-object category as ordinary modules over its section-ring sheaf using [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. The equivalence is the identity on underlying abelian sheaves and morphisms; by the universal properties of kernels, cokernels and colimits it preserves these, and hence cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms. Its degreewise extension therefore identifies the localizations defining the ordinary uncompleted derived categories. We may make all subsequent computations in these ringed-site module categories.

source.place: Tag 00YV (algebraic structures); passage to complexes is the localization universal property.

proof.text: For any of the three small ringed sites, filtered sheaf colimits are exact by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. For a diagram of complexes $L_t$, apply exactness to $0\to\ker d_t^q\to L_t^q\to\operatorname{im}d_t^q\to0$ and $0\to\operatorname{im}d_t^{q-1}\to\ker d_t^q\to H^q(L_t)\to0$. These give the natural identity $H^q(\varinjlim_t L_t)=\varinjlim_tH^q(L_t)$ for every integer $q$. Thus termwise filtered colimits preserve quasi-isomorphisms and a common cohomological lower bound. This also proves independence of the functorial representative choices used in the question.

The descending-chain condition on closed subsets implies the ascending-chain condition on opens. Every union of opens is a finite subunion: otherwise successive choices of an open not covered by the preceding finite union give a strictly ascending chain. Thus every open subset of $T$, and every open of an affine open of $T$, is quasi-compact. In particular $U\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $W\subset T$, so $j$ is quasi-compact. An open immersion is a monomorphism, since two maps into $U$ agreeing in $T$ agree as maps into the open subscheme; consequently its diagonal is an isomorphism and is quasi-compact. Thus $j$ is also quasi-separated. The recollement hypothesis is now satisfied. Its common-bound injective models show $Rj_*D^{\ge c}\subset D^{\ge c}$: a model zero below $c$ remains zero there after applying $j_*$ termwise. Its stated left t-exactness gives $Ri^!D^{\ge c}\subset D^{\ge c}$.

source.place: Tag 09BM (lemma-closed-immersion-complement-retrocompact-exact); elementary quasi-compactness check and the cited recollement bounds.

proof.text: To apply a theorem stated with a termwise bound to the present cohomological bound, replace each input $L$ functorially by $\tau_{\ge c}L$, with zero terms below $c$, term $\operatorname{coker}(d_L^{c-1})$ in degree $c$, and terms $L^r$ in degrees $r>c$. The natural projection $L\to\tau_{\ge c}L$ has $H^r$ equal to the identity for $r\ge c$ and is a quasi-isomorphism when $H^{<c}(L)=0$. Cokernels commute with colimits, so this replacement commutes with the termwise colimit. By step 2 all replacement maps, including their colimit, are quasi-isomorphisms. Hence it suffices to prove the comparisons for these termwise bounded diagrams; the maps remain those induced by the original cocone.

source.place: Tag 0118 (section-truncations), canonical cochain truncation tau_ge; displayed formula and its cohomology.

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image] to $f=j$, the ring sheaf $B_U$, and the termwise bounded diagram $(V_t)$ of step 4. Step 3 supplies quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. It gives $\varinjlim_tH^q(Rj_*V_t)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(Rj_*(\varinjlim_tV_t))$ for every $q$. Here the module-object $j_*$ is transport of the same sheaf pushforward followed by restriction of scalars along $B_T\to j_*B_U$, as specified by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. The derived functor of this composite is computed on $B_U$-module K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Use that same source-module resolution in the direct-image theorem: the resulting chain groups and differentials agree, with $B_T$ acting through $B_T\to j_*B_U$. Restriction of that target scalar action changes neither kernels, cokernels nor sheaf colimits; the forgetful comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] verifies this on underlying abelian sheaves and reflects invertibility. Thus the displayed maps are the maps for the precise $Rj_*$ of the item. By step 2 their sources equal $H^q(\varinjlim_tRj_*V_t)$, so the canonical derived comparison is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Both paragraphs: qcqs bounded direct-image continuity; coefficient action checked against module pushforward definitions.

proof.text:
For every $K\in D^{\ge c}(B_T)$, take the natural distinguished triangle $i_*Ri^!K\to K\to Rj_*j^*K\to i_*Ri^!K[1]$ of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. Apply [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] and then the exact sheaf functor $i^*$. Exactness makes $i^*H^q(L)=H^q(i^*L)$ by the kernel/image formula, and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ identifies the support term with $H^q(Ri^!K)$. In particular the resulting exact sequence has consecutive terms
$$H^{q-1}(i^*K)\to H^{q-1}(i^*Rj_*j^*K)\to H^q(Ri^!K)\to H^q(i^*K)\to H^q(i^*Rj_*j^*K).$$
This sequence is natural in $K$: the given triangles are natural and shift compatible, and each connecting map is the cohomology of their fourth map, followed by $H^r(L[1])=H^{r+1}(L)$. Thus the connecting-map square also commutes for every arrow of the diagram and for every arrow of its cocone.

source.place: Equations (3.3)-(3.4), Lemma 3.4; cohomology sequence as in Stacks Tag 05RS.

proof.text: Put $N=\varinjlim_tN_t$. Take the filtered colimit of the exact sequences in step 6 for $K=N_t$ and compare it with the sequence for $K=N$. Both rows are exact, the top by [lem-pc-module-filtered-colimits-tensor]. Naturality in step 6 gives a commutative diagram of five consecutive terms. The four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms: for the terms $i^*N_t$ use exactness and colimit preservation of $i^*$ from [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] and step 2; for the terms $i^*Rj_*j^*N_t$ first use the corresponding exactness and colimit preservation of $j^*$, then apply step 5 to $(j^*N_t)$, and finally apply $i^*$. The input $(j^*N_t)$ has the common lower bound $c$ because $j^*$ is exact. The middle vertical map is, by its cocone construction and step 2, $H^q$ of $\varinjlim_tRi^!N_t\to Ri^!N$.

source.place: Support fibre sequence (3.3)-(3.4); agent filtered-colimit comparison using Stacks Tag 03DB.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] to that five-term diagram in the abelian category of $B_Z$-module sheaves. Its first and fifth vertical maps, being isomorphisms, are respectively epimorphic and monomorphic; its second and fourth maps are isomorphisms. Therefore its middle map is an isomorphism for every integer $q$. This proves the closed-support comparison is a quasi-isomorphism and hence an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Together with step 5 and the bounds of step 3, this is every assertion. All maps were induced by the original cocones, so the proof also preserves the specified comparisons. No upper cohomology bound was used.
